# Sway bar end link adjustment

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Bolt custom adjustable rear sway bar end links onto the vehicle frame and adjust them evenly. [t57]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Bolt the rear sway bar into place.
2. Remove the existing end links from the assembly.
3. Set the sway bar at an angle between 10 and 20 degrees from horizontal.
4. Measure the center-to-center distance from the frame mount to the end link mount.
5. [Partial] Search for custom adjustable end links with lengths matching your measurement.
6. Order the correct bolt size of 10mm for the new hardware.
7. Bolt the top ends of the end links onto the vehicle frame.
8. Adjust both the top and bottom sections of each end link to reach the desired length evenly.
9. Tighten the jam nuts on both the top and bottom of the end links.
10. Bolt the adjusted end links securely to the sway bar.

_Procedure reported by [t57]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-reinstate-rear-sway-bar.11547/>_

## Parts

- [Partial] Custom adjustable rear sway bar end links, Whiteline or SuperPro: Must have correct bolt size of 10mm. [t57]

## Tips & gotchas

- Ensure the measured length falls roughly in between the available adjustment lengths for best fit. [t57]
- Use a torque wrench to avoid over-tightening, as specs are relatively low. [t57]
